prompt.context: Your client is a multi-specialty hospital in the United States offering emergency care, scheduled surgeries, labor and delivery services, diagnostic testing, lab work, and patient education. The hospital is experiencing a high turnover of nurses in the past 12 months. The client needs your advice on how to better retain nurses and reduce turnover.
prompt.question: How should the hospital better retain nurses and reduce turnover? The client's goal is to bring retention back to the pre-12-months level of 85%, with a strategic initiative(s) budget of $1M.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current retention/turnover rate?
clarifying_info.a: Current TTM retention rate is 70%; the target is 85%, so the delta is 15 percentage points.

clarifying_info.q: How is the competition doing on turnover?
clarifying_info.a: The competition is also facing high turnover, but the client's turnover rate is higher than the industry average.

clarifying_info.q: Is turnover a problem across all staff types?
clarifying_info.a: Turnover for doctors, technicians, and other administrative staff is lower than industry average and is not a concern. The issue is specific to nurses.

clarifying_info.q: What is the hospital's financial profile?
clarifying_info.a: Revenue of approximately $10M with 2% YoY growth for the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: Is increasing nurse wages an option?
clarifying_info.a: No, increasing wages is not an option.

exhibits.title: Wage Chart
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart comparing the client hospital and four competitors (Hos A, Hos B, Hos C, Hos D) on two dimensions: monthly pay in dollars (bar chart, right axis) and hours worked per week (line or dot, left axis).

exhibits.title: Nurse Pulse Survey
exhibits.shows: A heatmap or rating grid showing how nurses rank six preferences (Pay, Benefits, Career Advancement, Good Management, Schedule Flexibility, Continuing Education) and how each hospital (Client, Hos A, Hos B, Hos C, Hos D) scores on each preference relative to nurses' stated importance.

exhibits.title: Strategic Initiatives
exhibits.shows: A table listing four strategic initiatives with their TTM attrition drop under high adoption (>=80%) and low adoption (<80%), and the implementation cost for each initiative.

notes: Example of 80% adoption: for Mentorship Program, if adopted by 80%+ nurses, retention increase = 12%; else 4%
There is a certain probability of >80% adoption for each initiative

framework: Company: Current pay and benefits structure; schedule flexibility; patient volume MoM; patient mix; financial health (bonuses, rewards); relationships with insurers and partners
Employees: Work-life balance and sustainability; growth and learning opportunities; career path and promotion cycles; intrinsic motivation; feedback on management and leadership; turnover numbers MoM
External Factors: Competitive landscape offering better pay and benefits; other lucrative professions reducing nursing aspirants

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what can you infer about the client's nurse compensation situation relative to competitors?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute $/hr for each hospital and identify that the client has the highest hours per week (40) and the lowest $/hr. Strong candidates will note that simply raising wages is the obvious lever but should wait for the interviewer to confirm that wage increases are not an option before pivoting.

math.answer: Client's effective wage is $22/hr — the lowest among all five hospitals. The client also demands the most hours (40 hrs/week). Since wage increases are not an option, the focus must shift to other retention levers.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 2 (Nurse Pulse Survey), which two nurse preferences should the client prioritize to maximize retention impact?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Career Advancement and Schedule Flexibility as the two highest-priority areas: both are rated very important by nurses (top preferences) and the client lags competitors by approximately 75% on each. Pay should be acknowledged but set aside since wage increases are not an option. Continuing Education is another gap but is an industry-wide issue better addressed long-term. All other hospitals score well on Schedule Flexibility, lagging only ~25%.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, which initiative(s) should the client implement given the $1M budget and the need to increase retention by 15 percentage points (from 70% to 85%)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should: (1) ask for the adoption probabilities, (2) calculate weighted average attrition drops for each initiative, (3) enumerate feasible combinations within $1M, (4) check which combinations meet or exceed the 15% target. The recommended combination is Eliminating Mandatory Overtime + Digital Tool for Dynamic Scheduling: combined weighted drop = 5.0% + 11.0% = 16%, which exceeds the 15% target, at a combined cost of $250K + $700K = $950K — $50K under budget. Strong candidates note that additional capital ($100K–$200K) could fund further initiatives.

math.setup: Weighted Avg Attrition Drop = P(>=80%) x Drop(>=80%) + (1 - P(>=80%)) x Drop(<80%)
steps: Cross Department Rotation: 0.50 x 10% + 0.50 x 5% = 5.0% + 2.5% = 7.5% | Cost: $350K
Eliminating Mandatory Overtime: 0.75 x 6% + 0.25 x 2% = 4.5% + 0.5% = 5.0% | Cost: $250K
Digital Tool for Dynamic Scheduling: 0.375 x 16% + 0.625 x 8% = 6.0% + 5.0% = 11.0% | Cost: $700K
Combination check — Eliminating Overtime + Digital Scheduling: 5.0% + 11.0% = 16.0% >= 15% target; $250K + $700K = $950K <= $1M budget (passes)
Alternative: Cross Dept Rotation + Eliminating Overtime + Digital Scheduling: 7.5% + 5.0% + 11.0% = 23.5%; $350K + $250K + $700K = $1.3M — exceeds budget
Alternative: Mentorship + Eliminating Overtime: 10.0% + 5.0% = 15.0%; $800K + $250K = $1.05M — marginally over budget
Alternative: Mentorship + Cross Dept Rotation: 10.0% + 7.5% = 17.5%; $800K + $350K = $1.15M — over budget
math.answer: Recommended: Eliminating Mandatory Overtime ($250K, 5.0% weighted drop) + Digital Tool for Dynamic Scheduling ($700K, 11.0% weighted drop) = 16.0% total drop at $950K total cost. Meets the 15% retention target with $50K budget remaining.

brainstorming.prompt: Please provide the client with some ideas on how to improve career advancement and create schedules with better flexibility for nurses.

categories.name: Career Advancement
ideas: Standard promotion schedule with raises and bonuses for good performance
Path to management of other nurses or administrative/leadership roles
Mentorship program pairing junior nurses with senior nurses
Sponsorship for higher education (tuition reimbursement, continuing education)
Cross-department rotation program to broaden skills and career exposure

categories.name: Schedule Flexibility
ideas: Give nurses greater control over the number of hours worked per week
Allow more agency for nurses to self-select and pick their preferred shift hours
Implement an online/digital scheduling tool for real-time shift management
Improve lead time for management to communicate shift assignments in advance
Make it easier for nurses to change or drop shifts with minimal friction

recommendation: Invest in two initiatives: (1) Eliminating Mandatory Overtime ($250K) and (2) a Digital Tool for Dynamic Scheduling ($700K). Combined, these deliver an estimated 16% weighted average attrition drop, exceeding the 15-point retention target (from 70% to 85%+), within the $1M budget with $50K to spare.
risks: Nurses' preferences are dynamic and may shift, reducing the effectiveness of current initiatives
Adoption probability estimates are not concrete — actual adoption rates may differ from projections, changing the expected attrition drop
next_steps: Launch a pulse-check survey to validate nurse buy-in on the two recommended initiatives before full rollout
Allocate remaining ~$50K buffer and explore additional capital ($100K–$200K) to fund the Cross Department Rotation or Mentorship Program for incremental retention gains
Explore restructuring the pay model to move toward competitors' average hourly pay, even if total monthly pay stays flat (e.g., reduce mandatory hours to raise effective $/hr)
Pilot the digital scheduling tool in one department before hospital-wide deployment
